author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New England Coffee Cafe plans to reopen in Malden on Monday, September 14, ending a closure of nearly four months after a multi-vehicle crash damaged the Charles Street property.

The cafe at 108 Charles Street closed after the May 19 collision. Two people were hospitalized, and the impact forced repairs before the retail operation could welcome customers again. The company announced the reopening date this week.

The shop is part of a business with deep ties to the city. New England Coffee was founded in Boston in 1916 and moved its operations to Malden in 1966. Its flagship retail store opened in 1986, making the cafe a familiar stop for workers and residents near the company’s roasting operations.

The reopening restores a longstanding local storefront while marking another step in the property’s recovery from the crash. Customers should check the cafe’s current operating hours before visiting, as schedules can change during the first days after an extended closure.
dek: The Charles Street shop has been closed since a May vehicle crash damaged the building and hospitalized two people.
headline: New England Coffee Cafe sets September 14 reopening in Malden
